registration_file.description: File where the route / handler is *registered* (e.g., server.ts for app.post(...)). For file-based routing (Nuxt, Next), this equals handler_file.

handler_file.description: File containing the handler function body. For modular routing (e.g., Express app.post('/x', require('./routes/x'))), handler_file is routes/x.ts while registration_file is server.ts. Delta-mode invalidation keys off handler_file primarily.

line_range.description: [start_line, end_line] within `handler_file` (not `registration_file`). The handler body's line span, used as input to handler_hash.

serves_resource.description: Canonical data_model entity id this surface reads/emits, if any. Join key for the Authorized-Egress reconciliation (v2.4); v2.6 pairs it with `layer` — see below.

layer.description: v2.6 story 2.4. WHERE THIS SURFACE RUNS, and therefore who its caller is. The R5 gate floor is now computed per (serves_resource, layer), so a resolve-layer surface can only set the floor for sinks in its OWN layer. Measured failure this closes: a cron scheduler's resolve-layer surface set the floor for a resource, and a `console.log(JSON.stringify(summary))` in a developer's own CLI was filed as an under-gated byte path against it — 115 of 306 raw R-rule rows compared an HTTP RBAC gate to a cron HMAC gate on `emits_bytes:false` surfaces. Optional: validate-egress.py infers it from `category` (scheduler/queue_consumer ⇒ worker, cli_admin ⇒ cli, *_ipc ⇒ ipc), then the handler path, then the partition id, then defaults to `http`.

intended_gate.description: The strongest gate the served resource declares (RBAC / tenant-ownership / 2FA-share / OIDC). A resolve-layer surface that holds the real gate (e.g. a /s/{shortId} 2FA resolver) is how the cross-layer R5 rule finds the floor for byte-serving sinks IN THE SAME LAYER (v2.6).

gate_rank_hint.description: v2.6 story 2.7. The rank of `intended_gate`, stated structurally rather than inferred from its wording. AUTHORITATIVE — the keyword ranker is the fallback. Set it whenever the gate is real but does not read like `role`/`session`/`2fa`: unrecognised text ranks 0, and a rank-0 branch under a rank-2 floor is filed CRITICAL, so a rich and correct description was the worst case. See lib/sink-schema.json for the measured example.

emits_bytes.description: True if this surface itself returns the resource's bytes (a sink). False for resolve/identify surfaces that only hand out an id — those establish the gate floor but are not the egress.

guarded_paths.description: Per-branch authz, same shape as sink guarded_paths. Lets the reconciliation read this surface's enforced gate per branch.

gate_rank_hint.description: v2.6 story 2.7. Authoritative rank for `enforced_gate`; the keyword ranker is the fallback. See lib/sink-schema.json's branch-level field for the measured failure.
